<ConflictType> — Complementary information

The retrieved documents provide complementary information because they offer different facets of plumbing costs—such as national averages, regional rates (Florida, Texas, Pennsylvania, Toronto), hourly ranges, flat fees, and specific repair costs—without contradicting each other. Each snippet adds a piece (geographic scope, job type, pricing model) that together paint a broader picture.

The evidence collectively shows that plumbing costs vary widely by region, job type, and pricing model. d1, d4, d8, and d9 give national averages and hourly ranges [d1][d4][d8][d9], while d2, d3, d5, and d7 provide regional specifics for Toronto, Florida, Texas, and Pennsylvania [d2][d3][d5][d7]. d6 lists specific repair costs from a Houston company [d6]. None conflict; they complement each other by covering different scopes and cost components.

Based on the complementary evidence, the cost of a plumber is not a single number but depends on location, job complexity, and service type. Nationally, hourly rates typically range from $45 to $200, with an average around $105 per hour [d4][d8]. For small repairs, costs average $125–$350, while large repairs can be $500–$800 [d9]. Regional variations exist, such as $160–$180 for a service call in Toronto [d2] or $45–$200 per hour in Florida [d3]. Specific repairs like bathtub or faucet fixes range from $145 to $900 [d6]. Emergency or complex jobs cost significantly more [d1][d8].

The cost of hiring a plumber varies widely depending on location, job type, and urgency. Nationally, hourly rates typically range from $45 to $200, with an average around $105 per hour [d4][d8]. For small repairs like fixing a toilet or faucet, average costs are $125 to $350, while larger repairs average $500 to $800 [d9]. Regional examples include service calls costing $160–$180 in Toronto [d2], hourly rates of $45–$200 in Florida [d3], and average plumber costs of $180–$2,000 in Texas [d5]. Specific repair costs, such as bathtub repair ($145–$900) or garbage disposal repair ($150–$250), also illustrate the range [d6]. Emergency calls or complex jobs can cost significantly more, with emergency hourly rates averaging $350 [d8].
